answers.answer: Starting hands are 4 cards each for 2 players, 3 each for 3 players, and 2 each for 4 players. Remove the Epidemic cards and set them aside before shuffling/dealing the remaining City and Event cards. Matching pawns start in Atlanta.
answers.evidence: Setup: remove Epidemic cards; starting-cards table; place matching colored pawns in Atlanta.

answers.answer: Put the Infection Rate marker on the leftmost 2. Reveal 3 Infection cards and place 3 matching cubes in each named city; reveal 3 more and place 2 each; reveal 3 more and place 1 each. Put all 9 revealed cards face up on the Infection Discard Pile; the remaining cards form the Infection Deck.
answers.evidence: Setup, step 8: marker on leftmost ‘2’; three groups of three; revealed cards to discard pile, remaining cards form deck.

answers.answer: Use 4 Epidemics for Introductory, 5 for Standard, or 6 for Heroic; remove unused Epidemic cards from the game. Divide the remaining Player cards into that many face-down piles as equal in size as possible, shuffle one Epidemic into each pile, then stack the piles with smaller piles on the bottom.
answers.evidence: Setup, step 7: difficulty counts; equal as possible piles; one Epidemic per pile; smaller piles on bottom.

answers.answer: Take up to 4 actions; actions may be repeated and you may stop early. Action-cost cards go to the Player Discard Pile. Then draw 2 Player cards together (resolve any Epidemics, then get down to the 7-card limit), then Infect Cities. After all three phases, play passes to the left.
answers.evidence: Turn Structure and Actions: up to 4, may repeat/stop; discards to Player Discard Pile; phases in order; passes left.

answers.answer: Drive/Ferry moves along a white line to a connected city and costs no card. Direct Flight discards the destination city's City card. Charter Flight discards the City card matching the city you are currently in and moves to any city. Shuttle Flight moves from a city with a research station to any other city with one. White lines off a board edge wrap around to the other edge (example: Sydney and Los Angeles).
answers.evidence: Movement Actions table; Special Rules: Board wrapping.

answers.answer: Normally, spend the City card matching your current city, take a research station from the supply, and place it in that city. If all 6 are already built, relocate one from anywhere on the board. If the box supplied more than 6, set extras aside during setup.
answers.evidence: Other Actions: Build a Research Station; Special Rules: Research station limit and extras.

answers.answer: One Treat Disease action removes one cube of one chosen color. For a cured disease it removes all cubes of that one color in the city. Each different color takes a separate action; removed cubes return to the cube supply. Thus the two cured colors each require their own action to clear, and the uncured color is removed one cube per action.
answers.evidence: Other Actions: Treat Disease; one color per action; cubes returned to supply.

answers.answer: At any research station, discard 5 City cards of the same disease color (4 for the Scientist), then move that disease's cure marker to its Cure Indicator. The station city's color need not match. Existing cubes remain, and the disease can still infect until eradicated. If there are no cubes of that color anywhere on the board, it is immediately eradicated and the marker is flipped.
answers.evidence: Cure Procedure: any station, same-color cards, existing cubes remain; no cubes means immediate eradication and flip.

answers.answer: A player may give or take the City card matching the city both players occupy. Both players must agree. If the recipient exceeds 7 cards, they must immediately discard or play an Event card until within the limit.
answers.evidence: Other Actions: Share Knowledge; both agree; Hand Limit applies immediately after receiving via Share Knowledge.

answers.answer: The Researcher may give any City card from their hand to a player in the same city, on either player's turn. The exception transfers only from the Researcher to the other player; another player cannot use it to give an arbitrary nonmatching City card to the Researcher.
answers.evidence: Special Rules: Researcher exception states direction, any card, same city, either player's turn, and excludes arbitrary transfers to Researcher.

answers.answer: After actions, draw 2 Player cards together. If fewer than 2 cards remain when you need to draw, the game ends and players lose; do not reshuffle discards. The summary does not specify a separate loss timing for a deck with exactly one card remaining beyond saying fewer than 2 remain when the draw is needed.
answers.evidence: Drawing Player Cards: draw top 2 together; if fewer than 2 remain when needed, lose; do not reshuffle discards.

answers.answer: Increase the Infection Rate marker by one. For Infect, draw the bottom Infection card; add cubes of its color to the named city only up to 3. With two already there, add one to reach 3, then an outbreak occurs. Discard that Infection card to the Infection Discard Pile. For Intensify, shuffle only the Infection Discard Pile and place it on top of the Infection Deck. Remove the Epidemic card from the game and do not draw a replacement Player card.
answers.evidence: Epidemic Cards: Increase, bottom-card Infect adds only enough to reach 3 then outbreak, discard, Intensify; no replacement.

answers.answer: The Infection cards flipped at 0, 1, 2, 3, 4, 5, and 6 Epidemics are respectively 2, 2, 2, 3, 3, 4, and 4.
answers.evidence: Player Reference: Infection Rate Track table maps Epidemics resolved 0–6 to 2, 2, 2, 3, 3, 4, 4.

answers.answer: Resolve the first Epidemic completely through Increase, Infect, and Intensify, then resolve the second the same way. Events may be played between the two. Reduce an over-limit hand only after resolving any drawn Epidemic cards, by discarding or playing Events until at most 7.
answers.evidence: Epidemic Cards: two Epidemics resolve all steps for first then second and Events between; Hand Limit: first resolve drawn Epidemics.

answers.answer: Flip the top Infection cards, one at a time, equal to the current infection rate. For each, normally place one matching cube; if that disease is eradicated, place none; if the disease is cured but not eradicated, it can still receive cubes. If the city already has 3 cubes of that color, place no fourth and cause an outbreak. Discard each Infection card to the Infection Discard Pile.
answers.evidence: Infecting Cities: top of deck, rate number, one at a time, eradicated exception, 4th causes outbreak, discard pile; Cure Procedure: cured disease can still infect.

answers.answer: An outbreak adds one cube to every connected city, and any connected city already at 3 cubes outbreaks after the current outbreak resolves. The chain reaction is therefore resolved after the first outbreak; do not add cubes to cities that have already had an outbreak while resolving that Infection card, including the first city if the chain would return there. Each outbreak advances the marker one space. Cities may hold multiple colors, up to 3 cubes of each color.
answers.evidence: Outbreaks: chain reactions occur after current outbreak resolves; no cubes to cities already outbreaked on current card; marker advances; up to 3 of each color.

answers.answer: No. Airlift cannot be played after an Infection card is drawn but before resolving that card, because Events cannot be played between drawing and resolving a card. It can be played after that card resolves and before the next card is drawn/resolved; Events are not actions, the player using the Event chooses its use, and the played Event goes to the Player Discard Pile.
answers.evidence: Event Cards: any player, any time, not an action; cannot be played between drawing and resolving a card; player who plays chooses; discard to Player Discard Pile.

answers.answer: As an action, take one Event card from anywhere in the Player Discard Pile and store it on the Contingency Planner Role card. Capacity is one, and it does not count against the hand limit. When played, remove it from the game instead of discarding it.
answers.evidence: Roles: Contingency Planner ability specifies action, anywhere in Player Discard Pile, limit 1, no hand-limit count, and remove from game after play.

answers.answer: As an action, the Dispatcher may move any pawn to a city with another pawn, or move another player's pawn as if it were their own; moving another player's pawn requires that owner's agreement. Direct/Charter Flight cards come from the Dispatcher's hand; for Charter Flight, the card matches the moved pawn's departure city. The Dispatcher cannot direct another pawn to Treat Disease or take another nonmovement action, and cannot use the Operations Expert's special move.
answers.evidence: Roles: Dispatcher paragraph states options, agreement, action restriction, card payer/city, and Operations Expert restriction.

answers.answer: The team wins immediately upon discovering cures for all 4 diseases; eradication and a clear board are not required. The three losses are: the Outbreaks marker reaches the last space (8th outbreak); the required cubes of a color cannot be placed, causing an immediate loss during an epidemic, outbreak, or infection; or a player cannot draw 2 Player cards after actions because fewer than 2 remain.
answers.evidence: Scoring/Victory Conditions: Victory and three Defeat conditions; Cube supply check says immediate loss.

answers.answer: Put the board within reach and the 6 stations and separated disease cubes nearby; place one station in Atlanta. Put the Outbreaks marker on 0 and the four cure markers vial-side up near their indicators. Give each player a Reference card; shuffle Role cards and deal one face up to each; put matching pawns in Atlanta; remove unused Roles and pawns. The player with the highest-population City card goes first. The summary does not state a separate setup procedure for unused cure markers or board supplies beyond these instructions.
answers.evidence: Setup steps 1–5 and 9 specify supplies, station, markers, Role/Reference cards, unused roles/pawns, and first player.

answers.answer: Teammates may offer advice, but the active player decides their actions. Introductory hands are face up for all to see. Standard and Heroic hands are private by default, though experienced groups may choose open hands. Anyone may examine either discard pile at any time.
answers.evidence: Turn Structure: active player decides; Special Rules: hand display by difficulty and either discard pile inspectable.

answers.answer: Removing the last cube of a disease that is not cured does not eradicate it. If the last cube of a cured disease is removed, eradicate it and flip its cure marker to the eradication side. Eradicated diseases receive no new cubes during normal infections or Epidemics; cured but non-eradicated diseases can still receive them.
answers.evidence: Eradication bullets and Cure Procedure: uncured last cube has no effect; cured last cube flips marker; eradicated diseases get no new cubes.

answers.answer: For a non-eradicated disease with zero cubes in the named city, place 3 cubes. Reaching three does not itself cause an outbreak; outbreak occurs if the city already has 3 and another cube would be added. Discard the Infection card to the Infection Discard Pile before Intensify.
answers.evidence: Epidemic Cards: place 3 cubes, add only enough to reach 3 if cubes already exist then outbreak; discard card to Infection Discard Pile.

answers.answer: Increase still occurs. The Infect step still draws the bottom Infection card, but places no cubes if its disease is eradicated; the Infection card is discarded to the Infection Discard Pile. Intensify still reshuffles only that discard pile and puts it on top of the Infection Deck.
answers.evidence: Epidemic Cards: all three steps; Infection skips cubes if eradicated; card discarded; Intensify follows.

answers.answer: After the first Intensify, the Infection Discard Pile is empty. The second Epidemic's bottom card is therefore the only card shuffled in the second Intensify; it is placed on top. When normal Infections draw it, it names the city from that second Epidemic and normally causes an outbreak, since the city reaches 3 cubes from the Epidemic and no protection or eradication intervenes.
answers.evidence: Epidemic Cards: two-Epidemic sequence notes second bottom card is only card shuffled, ends on top, drawn first and normally causing outbreak.

answers.answer: The Scientist needs 4 same-color City cards instead of 5 to Discover a Cure. The cure still must be discovered at any research station; the station city's color need not match the disease color.
answers.evidence: Cure Procedure and Roles: Scientist needs only 4; station city color need not match.

answers.answer: As an action, the Operations Expert builds a research station in their current city without needing a City card; no card is held, used, or discarded for this build.
answers.evidence: Roles: Operations Expert can build a station in the current city as an action with no City card needed, used, or discarded.

answers.answer: Once per turn, as an action, the Operations Expert may move from a city with a research station to any city by discarding any City card. The card need not match a city; the summary states no other destination restriction.
answers.evidence: Roles: Operations Expert special move once per turn, as action, from a research station, any city, discard any City card.

answers.answer: The Medic's Treat Disease action removes all cubes of one chosen color from the city. It does not remove multiple colors in one action; each different color requires its own action.
answers.evidence: Roles: Medic Treat Disease removes all cubes of one color; Other Actions: each different color is a separate action.

answers.answer: When a cure is discovered while the Medic is already in a city, the Medic immediately removes all cubes there of that cured color, with no action needed. Later, when another player moves the Medic into another city with cubes of that cured color via Dispatcher or Airlift, the Medic automatically removes all those cubes upon entering, also with no action needed. The summary does not specify the number of cubes removed in that example beyond all cubes of the cured color.
answers.evidence: Roles: Medic paragraph says automatic all-cube removal on cure discovery while there and on entering via Dispatcher or Airlift, with no action needed.

answers.answer: The Medic prevents placement and outbreaks of cured diseases in the Medic's own city. This does not protect adjacent cities or uncured diseases.
answers.evidence: Roles: Medic prevents placement and outbreaks of cured diseases in Medic's city, not adjacent cities or uncured diseases.

answers.answer: The Quarantine Specialist prevents cube placement and outbreaks of every disease color in their current city and all connected cities. This ability does not affect cubes placed during setup.
answers.evidence: Roles: Quarantine Specialist protection area, all colors, setup exception.

answers.answer: Resilient Population removes any one card from the Infection Discard Pile from the game. It may be played between an Epidemic's Infect and Intensify steps, so it may remove the Infection card just discarded during that Epidemic before Intensify shuffles the discard pile.
answers.evidence: Event Cards: Resilient Population removes any card in Infection Discard Pile from game; may be played between Infect and Intensify.

answers.answer: One Quiet Night skips the next Infect Cities step, so no Infection cards are flipped for that step. It does not skip an Epidemic's Infect step.
answers.evidence: Event Cards: One Quiet Night description.

answers.answer: Airlift moves any one pawn to any city. If it is another player's pawn, get that player's permission.
answers.evidence: Event Cards: Airlift description.

answers.answer: Only Player cards count toward the seven-card limit. Role and Reference cards do not; an Event stored on the Contingency Planner Role card also does not count. The summary says to discard cards or play Event cards until at most 7, but does not specify which cards must be selected from a hand of nine.
answers.evidence: Hand Limit: Player cards only; Roles/Reference do not count; Roles: stored Event doesn't count; Hand Limit: discard or play Events to reduce.

answers.answer: Government Grant places a research station in any city, regardless of the player's location, without discarding a City card.
answers.evidence: Event Cards: Government Grant places a research station in any city with no card discard needed.

answers.answer: Forecast lets the player draw and view the top 6 cards of the Infection Deck, rearrange them, and put them back on top of that deck.
answers.evidence: Event Cards: Forecast description.
